summary: Daemon-only change (packages/daemon) implementing LEGION-107 per .legion/plan.json T1-T7 and the LEGION-101 Design contract: (1) `receipt_timeout` is accepted and, on a process that probes alive (root pane; worker's cached shim client or pane), logged once and otherwise ignored; (2) `delivery_failed`/`no_holder` on an alive root architect keep the reclaim directive but re-send through an in-memory `ResendLedger` keyed by the message (topic + payload), at most 3 re-sends with pauses 5/15/45 s before each (the first included), the root re-probed after the pause, each copy carrying the triggering exception's `dedupe_key` in the listener publish body, an exception during a pending pause dropped uncounted, one cap line, 5-minute TTL, pauses cancelled by `dispose()`; (3) `worker-queued` is published once, when a token joins the queue, and only for an architect assignment. No LegionDaemonApi/pane-contract bump (stays 2), no state schema change, the reclaim-architect directive JSON unchanged.

acceptance.1: P1 'receipt_timeout for a root architect whose pane probes alive publishes nothing, sends no directive, and logs one line naming the role token and event id'; P2 it.each 'resurrects a dead root architect on a %s exception' (no_holder, receipt_timeout).
acceptance.2: P3 'receipt_timeout for a phase worker with a connected shim client publishes nothing, prompts nothing, and leaves pendingAssignment and the queue unchanged'; P4 '... with no cached client but a live pane logs once and resumes nothing'; P5 '... whose socket and pane are gone follows the existing resume path'.
acceptance.3: P14 (spacing on the injected clock, three re-sends, cap line, dedupe key on every publishRole call); P6 'a different message starts its own re-send count, each re-send carrying its own exception's dedupe key'; P6b 're-sends a message whose exception carried no dedupe_key (an older listener) without one, logging dedupe key none'; P7 'drops, without counting, an exception for a message whose re-send pause is still running'; P8 'resurrects a root that dies during the re-send pause instead of directing it'; P9 'dispose() cancels a pending re-send pause so firing it afterwards sends nothing'; L1-L4 + clear() in resend-ledger.test.ts; I1 index.test.ts 'envoyPublishBody carries dedupe_key only when a key is given'.
acceptance.4: P10 'role-lane exceptions for a worker whose assignment is already queued at the cap add no worker-queued and no queue entry' (green before the change: resumeWorker already drops a catch-up behind a queued assignment; kept as the acceptance-line-4 regression lock); P11 'queues one catch-up and publishes no worker-queued when two role-lane exceptions name a busy live worker' (red before: two worker-queued); P12 'replaces an already-queued role's task on a second spawnWorker and publishes no second worker-queued' (red before); P13 'queues a catch-up the worker acknowledged without a turn and publishes no worker-queued for it' (red before); existing 'queues a second spawnWorker call at the running-worker cap and publishes worker-queued to the architect' unchanged.
acceptance.5: Existing reducers.test.ts tests cited, nothing added: 'ignores a status update whose seq is not newer than the last one applied to the issue'; 'applies a redelivered event with the same seq exactly once'; 'leaves status and children intact when an older issue.created is redelivered after a newer issue.updated'; the 'replays exactly once: <name>' loop over REPLAY_ONCE_CASES; 'leaves a released child in its parent's tree: todo under a live root emits no admit'; 'records a child and routes child-adopted to its active parent role' (child-adopted is emitted by issue.created only).
acceptance.6: P6-integration: P14 it.each 'integration: bounded re-sends for one message against an alive architect — $listener', both variants (a LEGION-108 listener honouring dedupe_key: receiver records 1 injection; a pre-LEGION-108 listener minting a fresh key per copy: 3 injections, the cap the only bound). No smoke rig, scratch daemon, throwaway broker, or scratch tmux server was run (Sami, 2026-09-13).

proof.criterion: Acceptance line 6 (and line 3's spacing and cap): a stream of delivery_failed exceptions for one message against an alive architect whose pane acknowledges the reclaim directive produces at most three re-publishes, each carrying the original dedupe_key in the publish call, then the cap log line; a receiver that drops copies by that key records exactly one injection.
proof.surface: The packages/daemon integration suite (fake tmux runtime answering a live pane, fake pane acknowledging every legion.ctl directive, injected manual clock, an in-test receiver modelling the plugin's dedupe by dedupe key) plus the pull request's CI. No smoke rig of any kind per Sami's standing order of 2026-09-13; the end-to-end proof is LEGION-101's production hour after the operator deploys.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && bun test src/daemon/__tests__/processes.test.ts -t "integration: bounded re-sends"  (both it.each variants); CI: Tests run 34820888723 (jobs lint, typecheck, test all success)
proof.observed: Both variants pass. Copies: exactly 3, each {subject: role topic, json: payload, dedupeKey: triggering exception's key} — variant 1 all publish.d1 (receiver injections: exactly [payload], copies 2 and 3 dropped by key); variant 2 publish.d1 / publish.fresh-2 / publish.fresh-3 (3 injections — the cap is the only bound before LEGION-108). Nothing sent before each pause fired on the clock (5000, 15000, 45000 ms); 3 controlRequests on legion.ctl.legion-42.1, each JSON exactly {type: reclaim-architect, issue, redeliver: {topic, payload, eventId: evt-k}} with no dedupeKey inside; three 're-sending event' lines naming token, evt-k, 'attempt k of 3', the copy's key; exactly one 're-send cap reached' line naming token, evt-4, and the fourth key; tree still {generation: 1, status: active}; no new-window/split-window. Full suite at d13ea8c9: 1281 pass, 10 skip (pre-existing), 0 fail.
proof.negativeControl: P14's fifth exception after the cap: the entry was dropped by the cap, so it is a new chain's attempt 1 — a 5000 ms wait appears and, without firing it, copies stay at 3 (nothing more is sent before the pause elapses); dispose() then cancels it and firing sends nothing. Also events.test.ts 'ignores an exception whose reason is not one of the three known ones': reason "timeout" reaches no recovery (exceptions array stays []).

proof.criterion: Acceptance lines 1 and 2: receipt_timeout on a live process (root pane; worker's cached client or live pane) publishes nothing, queues nothing, sends no directive, logs one line naming the role token and event id; a dead process follows the existing path.
proof.surface: packages/daemon unit suite (fake runtime, fake worker client) plus CI.
proof.observed: 6 pass: P1 (root alive: publications [], controlRequests [], one error line with token and evt-1, tree unchanged, no pane opened), P2 both reasons (dead root resurrected, generation 2), P3 (cached client: prompts [], publications [], queue still [token], claim deep-equal to its snapshot, one line), P4 (no cached client, live pane: zero socket dials, one line, claim untouched), P5 (socket and pane gone: --resume relaunch with catch-up queued, identical to no_holder).
proof.negativeControl: P5: the same receipt_timeout for a worker whose socket refuses and whose pane is gone takes the existing resume path (commands include --resume; pendingAssignment.kind === catchup) — liveness, not the reason, decides.

trickyParts: Rebase forced by a genuine CONFLICTING report: main had landed LEGION-103 (#1053, #1057) inside handleException, LEGION-15 (#1027) rewrote the processes.test.ts wait helpers (flushEventLoopUntil is gone; waits go through manager()'s sleeps(ms).next() observer), and #1050 reordered the worker queue (priority order, FIFO within a tier). Pre-rebase fingerprint a40758999f11d440a2abbf45363cdfccf2288b10115dc2019cf21b030660cf6f at b9c2948c; post-rebase e96834433269e90a1acfcfe5f92b01edc4272e377833870ae785ff423d6ceffe at d13ea8c9; changed on purpose (rebase comment on the PR).
main's manager() observer wrapper for publishRole dropped the third argument; it now forwards dedupeKey, or every dedupe-key assertion would have read undefined.

The reclaim-architect directive is built by destructuring {topic, payload, eventId} from exception.original — assigning the object whole would leak dedupeKey into the directive JSON (no excess-property check on a variable); P14 asserts the directive JSON never contains 'dedupeKey'.
manualSleep().fire(5_000) resolves the oldest 5000 ms wait; the worker prompt's turn-start bound is also 5000 ms, so no test combines an architect re-send with a worker prompt.
The existing 'reclaims a live root architect' and 'reports a reclaim-architect nack' tests now inject sleep: async () => {} — with a real timer they would wait the 5 s first pause.
deviations: LEGION-103's daemon stopgap on main (ignore every delivery_failed on an alive holder, logged once per role per 30 min; cap no_holder republishes per role token per 30 min while still sending the directive every time) is superseded by LEGION-101's fixed contract and removed: MAX_ROLE_REDELIVERIES, ROLE_REDELIVERY_PERIOD_MS, roleRedeliveries, noteLateReceipt, countRoleRedelivery, countRedelivery, and the three tests 'stops republishing one role message ... after MAX_ROLE_REDELIVERIES', 'treats a delivery_failed to a live architect as a late receipt', 'treats a delivery_failed to a worker whose shim client is connected as a late receipt'. Reported to the architect by envoy_publish (message eb19532efe7a8a44840d3355af8f2912). Consequence before LEGION-108 deploys: a slow holder's delivery_failed yields up to three paused copies (5/15/45 s, dedupe-keyed) instead of LEGION-103's zero; after it deploys, delivery_failed means a forward that never happened and gets the bounded re-send, which LEGION-103 would have dropped.
Plan D1 (ledger keyed by topic+payload, not event id) and D2 (pause before the first re-send too) as recorded in .legion/plan.json; both match the spec at version 4+.
The bookmark was set at @- rather than @ so the stray untracked .omp/config.yml in the working copy never entered a commit (plan T7).
openQuestions: Whether the architect wants LEGION-103's worker-side guard (delivery_failed with a cached shim client -> log, no catch-up) kept as an additive branch. The plan and spec route a worker's delivery_failed through resumeWorker (acceptance line 4 / P11: one catch-up queued silently); I followed the plan.
